title: Sass
description: Use Dart Sass with variables, nesting, mixins, and the modern @use module system.

data.text: Sass is a CSS preprocessor that compiles to plain CSS. It adds variables, nesting, mixins, functions, and a module system — features useful in large stylesheets that lack component scoping.

data.title: Install and compile
data.content: The `sass` package is the actively maintained Dart implementation; node-sass is deprecated.
data.code:
npm install -D sass
npx sass src/styles/main.scss dist/styles/main.css --style=compressed
npx sass --watch src/styles:dist/styles

data.caption: src/styles/button.scss — use the module

data.text: `@import` is deprecated because it leaks every variable into the global namespace and duplicates output. `@use` gives each file a private namespace (aliased with `as`), and `@forward` re-exports a module so a public API file can gather several partials.

data.caption: src/styles/index.scss — a public API entry point

data.title: darken() and lighten() are deprecated
data.text: Dart Sass moved colour functions to the `sass:color` module. `darken($c, 10%)` still compiles today but warns; the modern form is `color.adjust($c, $lightness: -10%)` or `color.scale($c, $lightness: -10%)`.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Know that `sass` (Dart Sass) replaced `node-sass`, that `@use` replaced `@import`, and that native CSS now supports variables and nesting — so the remaining reasons to add Sass are mixins and compile-time logic.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Pick Dart Sass (`npm i -D sass`); node-sass is deprecated.
Native CSS covers nesting and variables, so justify Sass by mixins and functions.
data.takeaway: Sass questions are usually really about migration: know the modern syntax, not just the old tutorials.
